newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCCER-COLOMBIA NOT THE SAME WITHOUT VALDERRAMA, SAYS COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCCER-COLOMBIA NOT THE SAME WITHOUT VALDERRAMA, SAYS COACH.

text.p: Colombia coach Hernan Dario Gomez, who brought a new-look experimental side to the Copa America after years of standing by the same players, said Saturday the team was not the same without the veterans.
An emotional Gomez, upset at comments that the older players were past their best, said Colombia's Copa America's performances were proof that he had been right to stick with them for so long.
In particular, Gomez said, the team had missed 36-year-old Carlos Valderrama, who was rested for the Copa America but is still a regular international.

"The team hasn't played well, we have not had personality, objectivity, I don't know if we are more worried about our opponents or about playing without Carlos Valderrama," he said after Colombia's 2-1 quarter-final defeat against Bolivia, their third loss in four games.
"For all this, Bolivia deserved to win and reach the semi-finals."

Colombians have been clamouring for a rebuilding of the national team, which has changed remarkably little over the last ten years with players such as Carlos Valderrama, Freddy Rincon, Leonel Alvarez and Faustino Asprilla becoming almost permanent fixtures.

The players have come from a generation which has lifted Colombia from soccer obscurity into a team that is respected worldwide. Colombia have qualified for the last two World Cups, although without delivering what the talent of the players has promised.
However, many now feel they have been in the national team too long.
"More than ever today, the players who everyone wanted to kick out, who they said were over the hill, are the ones who we must turn to," said Gomez.
"This (the Copa America team) is the team that the Colombian people asked for, a team that everybody believed in because it is a team that doesn't have Carlos Valderrama and the others."
"The lads we brought here are very capable but there is an awful long way to go before they can be anything like the older players."
"In Colombia, there was a brilliant era from '87 to '97 but I don't know if we can repeat this, there is a future but I don't know when the future will start giving us good results again," he said.
"Our campaign has been mediocre. I don't know if the country can stand three defeats in four games," he said, clearly implying it would be back to the older players for the World Cup qualifiers.

Colombia began their World Cup qualifying campaign well but have slipped recently with a run of three defeats and a draw in their last four games, prompting a wave of discontent among the fans. However, they are still third in the group and well-placed to qualify for France next year.
